_description: Software supply-chain attacks: malicious package uploads (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Crates.io, Maven), trojanized GitHub repos, package typosquats, and post-install script abuse. Detects discussion of fresh supply-chain incidents which are typically broadcast quickly in TI circles.

rules._description: Malicious package upload on a public registry. Two-signal lookahead: registry/ecosystem mention + malicious/trojan/backdoor framing.
rules._fp_risk: Low-medium. Threat-research blogs use similar language - excludes pin Socket/Phylum/Snyk research framing.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - supply-chain compromises affect every downstream user automatically.
rules.name: Supply chain - malicious package upload

rules._description: Typosquat / dependency-confusion package targeting a known popular library. Two-signal lookahead: registry mention + typosquat/lookalike/dependency-confusion language.
rules._severity_rationale: High - typosquat packages auto-distribute via developer copy/paste mistakes.
rules.name: Supply chain - typosquat / dependency confusion package

rules._description: Compromised maintainer / hijacked package. Two-signal lookahead: package/repo language + hijack/compromise/takeover framing.
rules._fp_risk: Low-medium. GitHub takeover stories in news fire - excludes pin obvious news framing.
rules._severity_rationale: Critical - maintainer hijack injects malicious code into legitimate, trusted packages.
rules.name: Supply chain - maintainer / package hijack

rules._description: Trojanized GitHub repository - fake security tool, fake PoC, fake hack-tool that includes malware. Common attack vector against security researchers.
rules._fp_risk: Medium. Researchers discuss trojanized repos with similar language - excludes pin research framing.
rules._severity_rationale: High - trojanized repos compromise the security community itself.
rules.name: Supply chain - trojanized github repo / fake PoC

rules._description: Post-install / setup.py / npm-postinstall abuse - when discussion mentions package install scripts being used as attack vectors. Two-signal lookahead: install-hook term + malicious/payload term.
rules._fp_risk: Low. Install-hook + malicious is distinctive vocabulary.
rules._severity_rationale: High - install-hook execution is silent, runs with developer privileges.
rules.name: Supply chain - install-script payload
